div.p: A Young, Skilled and Diverse Workforce Building a World-Class African City.

At the City of Joburg Property Company (JPC), our Human Capital Department is the engine behind an inclusive, high-performing and future-ready organization. We are committed to cultivating a workplace that reflects the diversity of Johannesburg’s population and aligns with the City’s long-term developmental vision—Joburg 2040.
With 68% of our employees being female and a majority aged between 31 and 40, our workforce represents a dynamic, capable pool of young professionals who are ready to innovate and lead.

JPC is guided by the principles of the Employment Equity Act to ensure equal access to opportunities for all South Africans. Through our Employment Equity and Skills Development (EESD) Forum, we drive organisational change and embed equity at all levels.

ul.li: Inclusive EESD Forum with representatives across all departments and regions.

div.p: These efforts are supported by numerical targets and affirmative action measures without establishing absolute barriers for non-designated groups, in line with Section 15(4) of the EEA.
To support JPC’s growth and transformation goals, we are implementing a range of forward-thinking initiatives:

ul.li: Culture and LeaderShift Programme to embed ethical leadership and high-performance values
Digital HR Solutions such as online career portals and high-potential assessments
Competency Frameworks to identify and build critical and scarce skills
Labour Consultations to foster sound employee relations

section.class: s_text_block pt40 pb40 o_colored_level o_cc o_cc4

div.p: Find answers to common questions about our workforce diversity, development programmes, and employment equity initiatives.

span.font: What is the role of the Human Capital Department at JPC?

div.p: The Human Capital Department manages employee recruitment, development, retention, and performance to support the strategic goals of JPC. It ensures a diverse, skilled and high-performing workforce aligned with the City of Johannesburg’s transformation and service delivery objectives.

span.font: How does JPC promote Employment Equity and diversity in the workplace?

div.p: JPC follows a formal Employment Equity Policy guided by the Employment Equity Act. The organisation uses both numerical targets and inclusive processes, including affirmative action measures and the Employment Equity and Skills Development Forum, to promote workplace diversity without creating absolute employment barriers.

span.font: What training and development opportunities are offered to JPC employees?

div.p: JPC offers a wide range of training initiatives, including leadership development, digital skills training, and job-specific upskilling. Each employee has a personalized Individual Development Plan (IDP) to ensure training aligns with personal growth and company needs.

span.font: How does JPC support youth employment and skills development?

div.p: Through initiatives such as internships, bursaries, and youth-focused training programmes, JPC empowers young professionals aged 31–40—who make up the majority of the workforce—to grow into future leaders while contributing to inclusive economic development.

Employee development is central to our mandate. In the 2024/25 period alone, over 397 employees received targeted training to close competency gaps and build internal capacity for future leadership roles.
We also maintain individual development plans (IDPs) to ensure all training aligns with both personal and organizational goals.
The Human Capital Department plays a key role in shaping an organizational culture where innovation, fairness, and collaboration thrive. Our culture initiatives aim to:

ul.li: Promote psychological safety and ethical leadership
Position JPC as an employer of choice in the public property sector

div.p: The JPC uses the scorecard approach to performance management in line with the group performance management framework of the City of Johannesburg.

In accordance with local government legislation, the Member of the Mayoral Committee (MMC) for Economic Development—as the political head of the sector in which JPC operates—is accountable to the City Council for programme performance. The MMC is responsible for overseeing the implementation of JPC’s business plan and performance scorecard.
In line with the Companies Act, JPC’s Board of Directors is accountable to the shareholder, represented by the Executive Mayor, for delivering on the company’s strategic and operational objectives.

div.p: City of Joburg Property Company Promotion of Access to Information Act Manual, 2018.

This Manual has been compiled for the City of Joburg Property Company in accordance with Section 14 of the Act. The purpose of the Act is to give effect to the public’s right to access information held by public and private bodies, as provided in Section 32 of the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, Act No. 108 of 1996 (as amended) (“the Constitution”), which states:
​“32 (1) Everyone has the right of access to—
(a) any information held by the state; and
(b) any information held by another person that is required for the exercise or protection of any rights.”
